User left a Lambda Labs GH200 instance running after brief testing and was billed $583 for 391 hours. Lambda's support said: 'Lambda does not distinguish between idle and in use instance states, so any time a running instance is attached... will be billed for.' User called it '390x overbilling' and said Lambda seemed to not care.

A developer built an unofficial CLI and MCP server for Lambda cloud GPU instances, enabling AI agents to find, launch, and terminate Lambda GPU instances (e.g. 'launch an H100, ssh in, run a job'), with Slack/Discord/Telegram notifications when instances are SSH-ready.

A developer built an unofficial Rust CLI and MCP server for Lambda cloud GPU instances. It lets AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor) find, launch, and terminate instances, e.g. "launch an H100, ssh in, and run big_job.py". It also sends Slack/Discord/Telegram notifications when an instance is SSH-ready and supports 1Password for API keys.

A user signed up for Lambda Labs to try a GH200 instance unavailable on Colab. They used it for about an hour in Jupyter, forgot to terminate it, and got a $583 bill for 391 hours. Support said Lambda doesn't distinguish idle from in-use instances, and the user felt they didn't care.

The same user suggested that Lambda Labs auto-stop or limit instances by default to prevent surprise bills. Support didn't respond to the suggestion, and the user was considering a chargeback through their bank.
